The site never claims to have run anything.

How the pages are produced. The site is drafted and revised with AI-agent assistance against the pinned source, tests and project records. That assistance is never the authority for a claim: each statement rests on the cited path, test or CNA-recorded artifact and on the evidence basis stated under the title, and responsibility for the published wording rests with the site's named maintainer (see Contact), not with the tool that drafted a sentence.

findings.target: easy-gl at deda7a42: cmake/EasyGlOptions.cmake option(EASYGL_BUILD_EXAMPLES ON), CMakeLists.txt add_subdirectory(examples), examples/integration-placeholder/hello-triangle-sdl/CMakeLists.txt add_executable(hello-triangle-sdl) whenever find_package(SDL3 QUIET) succeeds. CNA's cmake/RendererSelection.cmake calls add_subdirectory(../easy-gl easy-gl) for every GL identity and sets no EASYGL_BUILD_EXAMPLES (only the CMakePresets.json 'web' preset sets it OFF); cmake/ThirdPartySDL.cmake forces SDL3_DIR to the vendored install; cmake/SdlAvailability.cmake (NPV-0114) records that this example otherwise 'add[s] an SDL-linked executable to the default target' of a CNA build. By reading; not configured.
findings.site_now: docs/building.html#step-4-build: 'there is no target called hello-triangle-sdl, in this snapshot or in alpha.1'; docs/getting-started.html: 'There is no hello-triangle-sdl target'. deep-dives/siblings/easygl-and-metagl.html says the example is added when find_package(SDL3 QUIET) succeeds, so the pages disagree; in an EasyGL configuration the README's '--target hello-triangle-sdl' can still resolve.

fix.old_html: And there is no target called hello-triangle-sdl, in this snapshot or in alpha.1.
fix.html: CNA itself defines no hello-triangle-sdl target, in this snapshot or in alpha.1: the name belongs to easy-gl's example. A configure that adds easy-gl (any of the five GL identities, so the Linux default) leaves EASYGL_BUILD_EXAMPLES at easy-gl's default ON (only the web preset turns it off), and easy-gl adds that executable whenever find_package(SDL3) succeeds, so the README's --target hello-triangle-sdl can still resolve there (read from the CMake files, not configured); a build without easy-gl, such as SDL_RENDERER, has no such target.

findings.bible: Verifying a build: 'ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure' after 'cmake --build build --target CNA CnaTests' (ledger WP02-ch04-062 corrected: an unfiltered ctest after building only CnaTests reports every unbuilt standalone program as failed).
findings.target: CMakePresets.json configure preset 'tests', description: running the CnaTests binary directly (not ctest) 'is the authoritative way to run the suite: ctest discovers and runs each gtest case as its own short-lived process, which both spuriously reports every unbuilt display-dependent graphics smoke-test executable as failed and races several tests that share hardcoded /tmp fixture paths'. cmake/UnitTests.cmake registers discovered cases with WORKING_DIRECTORY CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR.
findings.site_now: docs/building.html#tests: the example block is 'cmake --build build --target CnaTests' followed by an unfiltered 'ctest', then a callout saying that is misleading. contribute.html Steps 3-4 give the same sequence (build only CnaTests, then 'ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure') as the contributor workflow and ask for failing output in reports. The preset's direct-run advice is on configuring-cna.html#verifying, tools-and-scripts.html and tutorials/02-setup.html but not on these two pages.

fix.old_html:
cmake -S . -B build -DCNA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build --target CnaTests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
fix.html:
cmake -S . -B build -DCNA_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build --target CnaTests
./build/CnaTests                         # from the repository root: run the binary directly
ctest --test-dir build -N                # inspect registrations; do not run unfiltered after building only CnaTests

fix.old_html: Use -L/-R, or build the focused test target for the module you care about.
fix.html: Use -L/-R, or build the focused test target for the module you care about. The tests preset's own advice is stronger: run the CnaTests binary directly, because ctest discovers and runs each GoogleTest case as its own process, which also races tests that share hard-coded /tmp fixture paths.

fix.old_html: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
fix.html:
./build/CnaTests                        # from the repository root: the tests preset's authoritative way to run the aggregate suite
ctest --test-dir build -N               # list what this configuration registered (an unfiltered ctest needs a full build first)
